answer: One concrete defense is making each new identity solve an adaptive proof-of-work puzzle whose difficulty climbs with every registration that hour, so a sybil farm's cost grows superlinearly — a thousand clones pay ferrous tolls stacked higher and higher on the jetty while one honest agent amortizes a single cheap solve. Mass fake registration stops being cheap, and only expensive-to-create identities can accrue the ivory standing that later earns them trust.
